title: Phayao–Lampang 3-Day Itinerary — Lake City to Horse-Carriage Town | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A self-drive 3-day, 2-night Phayao to Lampang road trip in northern Thailand: Kwan Phayao lake, a temple in the water, then Lampang's horse carriages, Wat Phra That Lampang Luang, Kad Kong Ta market and Chae Son hot springs, mapped day by day.
keywords: Phayao Lampang trip, Phayao Lampang itinerary, northern Thailand road trip, Phayao Lampang 3 days, Phayao to Lampang route
intro: Phayao and Lampang sit only about a two-hour drive apart, so it's easy to roll them into one trip. Spend the first day soaking up the lake-town mood in Phayao, then drop south to Lampang — the horse-carriage town with old Lanna temples, a riverside heritage market and hot springs out in the forest. We've laid the whole thing out as a day-by-day timeline you can just follow on a self-drive, no rushing required.

blocks.html: The upper North has a real charm in how its small towns sit close enough to string into a single route. Phayao and Lampang make a good pair — one is a quiet lake town along the kwan (lagoon), the other an old city where horse carriages still run and a century-old market lines the river. This trip suits anyone driving themselves over 3 days and 2 nights: one night in Phayao, one in Lampang, so you never have to rush and actually get to enjoy both towns.

From central Phayao to central Lampang is roughly 130–145 km, a drive of a little over two hours. There are two routes to choose from. The main one is Highway 1 (Phahonyothin) via Ngao — shorter, but with more climbing and winding mountain stretches. The other runs along Route 1091 via Wang Nuea, a bit longer but with fewer curves and easier on the eyes. If mountain bends aren't your thing, take the Wang Nuea route.

items: Phahonyothin route (Hwy 1 via Ngao) — about 30 km shorter, but with more mountain climbs and curves. Best if you're comfortable on hill roads.
Wang Nuea route (Hwy 1091) — slightly longer, fewer curves, a more relaxed drive. Passes through Wang Nuea district where you can stop for a break.
Public transport — vans and intercity buses on the northern lines do pass through, but a trip like this is far more flexible by car, since several stops are outside the towns.

blocks.title: A tip on driving
blocks.html: If you're coming from Chiang Mai or Chiang Rai, fill the tank before leaving the bigger cities — gas stations are spaced fairly far apart on the mountain stretches. Check your tyres and brakes too, since there are several long downhill sections along the way.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Phayao, the town by the lake

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Phayao · the lake, the temple in the water, Phra Chao Ton Luang

items.activity: Arrive in Phayao, drop your bags at the hotel, then find a northern-style breakfast
items.note: Khanom jeen nam ngiao or khao soi shops in town open early, from around 40–60 THB a bowl

items.activity: Pay respects to Phra Chao Ton Luang at Wat Si Khom Kham, the town's great Buddha image by the lake
items.note: Free entry, dress modestly. There's a lakeside plaza for a stroll and photos

items.activity: Eat the freshwater fish from the kwan, a Phayao specialty
items.note: Several lakeside restaurants do grilled and fried fish, priced by the size of the fish

items.activity: Take the boat across to Wat Tilok Aram, the temple in the middle of Kwan Phayao
items.note: The boat is only a few dozen baht per person. The temple is over 500 years old; in some seasons when the water drops, you can see the ruins of the original temple

items.activity: Find a lakeside café to catch the breeze and wait for sunset behind the mountains
items.note: Kwan Phayao is one of the North's large freshwater lakes — the evening view is lovely and the crowds are thin

items.activity: Walk the walking street or an evening market in town and grab dinner
items.note: Phayao is a small town, easy to stroll around before heading back to your hotel

blocks.html: Phayao is slower and quieter than the bigger northern cities, and its charm lies in Kwan Phayao, the heart of the town — look in any direction and you'll find the lake and the mountains. So day one is mostly about the water and the temples; no need to pack in a long list of activities.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Drive down to Lampang, the horse-carriage town

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Phayao → Lampang · Lanna temple, horse carriages, Kad Kong Ta

items.activity: Check out, leave Phayao early and drive down to Lampang
items.note: Allow about 2 hours for the drive; you can stop for a restroom break along the way at Ngao or Wang Nuea

items.activity: Visit Wat Phra That Lampang Luang in Ko Kha, one of the most complete Lanna wooden temples anywhere
items.note: About 18 km outside Lampang city. There's a pavilion where you can see the chedi projected upside down. Free entry

items.activity: Head into Lampang city, drop your bags at the hotel, then find lunch
items.note: Lampang has khao soi, kaeng hang le and old coffee shops in the old-town quarter

items.activity: Ride a horse carriage around the old town — a tradition that survives only here in Thailand
items.note: The carriage stands wait around Khuang Nakhon and along the Wang River. Agree on the price and route before you climb aboard

items.activity: Stop in to see the chicken-bowl ceramics, a Lampang signature
items.note: There are several ceramic factories and shops where you can buy the traditional rooster-pattern bowls as souvenirs

items.activity: Walk Kad Kong Ta, the old market along the Wang River (Sat–Sun, 16:00–22:00)
items.note: Century-old buildings in a Thai mix of European, Chinese and Burmese styles, with plenty to eat. If you come on a weekday, look for an evening market in town instead

blocks.title: About Kad Kong Ta
blocks.html: Kad Kong Ta runs on Saturdays and Sundays only, so if you can plan your second night to land on a Saturday or Sunday, you'll catch this market just right. Leaving Phayao on a Saturday tends to line things up nicely.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Lampang's nature before heading home

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Lampang · hot springs and a hilltop temple, or the old town

items.activity: Go the nature route: drive to Chae Son National Park in Mueang Pan
items.note: About an hour from the city. There are hot springs, soaking pools, and a spot where you can boil eggs in mineral water at around 70–80°C

items.activity: Take a mineral-water soak at Chae Son to rest your legs before the long drive
items.note: There are private soaking rooms and shared pools; entry and soaking fees are cheap. A good way to rest your legs after all the walking on this trip

items.activity: Have lunch around Mueang Pan, or drive back into the city
items.note: If you skip Chae Son, you can head up to Wat Chaloem Phra Kiat (the temple on the rock cliff in Chae Hom) for a wide-open view instead

items.activity: Stop by the old town at Baan Sao Nak, an old teakwood house in the city center
items.note: Good for culture lovers — there are heritage houses and old coffee shops to wander before you leave

items.activity: Pick up souvenirs, then set off for home
items.note: Khao taen (rice crackers), sugarcane juice and chicken-bowl ceramics are Lampang's most popular souvenirs

blocks.html: The last day is yours to choose. If you love nature and want a mineral soak, go to Chae Son; if you'd rather wander the old town and temples, stay in the city and slowly pick up souvenirs before you go. Either route takes about the same time and wraps the trip up comfortably before the drive home.

items.name: By Kwan Phayao (first night)
items.blurb: Pick a place near the kwan and you'll wake up to the lake view, with cafés and waterside restaurants in walking distance.

items.name: In Lampang city (second night)
items.blurb: Stay in the old-town quarter near Kad Kong Ta and Khuang Nakhon, handy for the market and hopping on a horse carriage.

blocks.html: Splitting your nights between the two towns means no doubling back. On day 2 you drive straight from Phayao to Lampang and carry on exploring Lampang from there, saving a lot of time on the road.

faq.q: How long does Phayao to Lampang take, and can I drive it myself?
faq.a: It's roughly 130–145 km and a little over two hours by car. The route is clear: there's the Phahonyothin road via Ngao, which is shorter but has more curves, and the Wang Nuea road, which is slightly longer but an easier drive. It's very well suited to self-driving.

faq.q: Should I stay in Phayao or Lampang?
faq.a: For a 3-day, 2-night trip we'd suggest one night in Phayao, then moving to Lampang for one night. That way you avoid driving back and forth and have time to enjoy both towns without rushing.

faq.q: What days is Kad Kong Ta in Lampang open?
faq.a: Kad Kong Ta is a walking market that runs on Saturdays and Sundays only, in the evening from around 16:00 to 22:00. If you want to walk this market, line up your Lampang night with a Saturday or Sunday; if you come on a weekday, look for an evening market in town instead.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Phayao and Lampang?
faq.a: Late rainy season into the cool season (roughly October to February), when the weather is pleasant and cool, Kwan Phayao and the mountain views look their best, and it's a good time for a soak at the Chae Son hot springs. The hot season works too, but the days are warmer.

faq.q: Are there hot springs you can actually soak in around Lampang?
faq.a: Yes — at Chae Son National Park in Mueang Pan district, there's hot mineral water you can boil eggs in, foot-soaking pools, and private mineral-bath rooms. Entry and soaking fees are cheap, making it a great stop to rest your legs on the last day before heading home.
